nodes.name: Long-reach EML/DFB laser diodes (1310nm for coherent modules)
nodes.description: Externally-modulated laser (EML) and distributed-feedback (DFB) laser diodes operating at 1310nm wavelength, used in coherent optical transceivers for long-reach datacenter interconnect (10+ km), especially in new high-capacity modules (800G+, 1.6T coherent). These differ fundamentally from short-reach 850nm VCSELs: they enable longer reach but have constrained manufacturing capacity concentrated in 4 vendors globally. The 2024–2025 shortage was a documented supply bottleneck.

metrics.name: EML/DFB laser wavelength (coherent datacom standard)
metrics.description: 1310nm is the standard C-band window for coherent optical transceivers in long-reach datacenter applications per ITU-T and OIF specifications.

metrics.name: Global EML/DFB laser supplier concentration (top-3 share)
metrics.description: Top 3 suppliers (Lumentum, Coherent, Mitsubishi Electric) control approximately 70–75% of datacom EML/DFB output; constrained by fab capacity.

metrics.name: EML/DFB laser capacity expansion lead time
metrics.description: Adding capacity for EML/DFB lasers requires dedicated epitaxial-growth tools, waveguide processing, and packaging qualification; typical expansion lead time 18–24 months.

nodes.notes: EML/DFB lasers are a separate supply chain from VCSEL arrays. The 2024–2025 optical transceiver shortage was partly driven by constrained EML capacity as demand shifted toward coherent (long-reach) module designs. If long-reach transceiver demand doubles, EML laser supply becomes critical path.

nodes.name: Lumentum Holdings Inc.
nodes.description: Leading US supplier of optoelectronic components and subsystems for datacenter, 5G, and coherent optical networks. Manufactures laser diodes (EML/DFB for coherent), photodetectors, and optical subassemblies. Primary supplier to Cisco, Infinera, Broadcom, and optical module makers.

metrics.name: Lumentum datacom/coherent optics revenue share
metrics.description: Estimated 28% market share in coherent optical module laser devices (EML/DFB) for 2024; source: analyst estimates from Yole Développement and SemiAnalysis industry reports.

metrics.name: Lumentum FY2025 revenue (fiscal year ended Sept 2025)
metrics.description: Lumentum FY2025 total revenue approximately $1.41 billion, with strong growth from datacenter optics segment per Q3/Q4 2025 earnings calls.

nodes.notes: Lumentum is listed on NASDAQ under ticker LITE. Strong exposure to datacenter buildout growth; primary supplier of EML/DFB lasers to Coherent, Infinera, and module makers. Investor relevance: direct beneficiary of long-reach transceiver scaling.

nodes.name: Coherent Corp (formerly Coherent Inc. + II-VI merger)
nodes.description: Leading global supplier of coherent optical transceivers, laser diodes (EML/DFB, VCSEL), photodetectors, and integrated optical subsystems. After 2024 merger/integration of II-VI (photodetectors, VCSEL) and Coherent (coherent transport), the company is a vertically integrated major player in long-reach and short-reach datacom optics.

metrics.name: Coherent datacom optics market share (EML/DFB + VCSEL combined)
metrics.description: Combined EML/DFB and VCSEL/photodiode share from Coherent Corp divisions estimated at 32% of datacom optical component market in 2024–2025, per analyst consensus.

metrics.name: Coherent FY2024 revenue
metrics.description: Coherent Corp FY2024 total revenue approximately $3.24 billion, with significant datacom optics contribution; 2024 full-year financials.

nodes.notes: Coherent Corp listed on NASDAQ (COHR). Major player in both long-reach (EML/coherent modules) and short-reach (VCSEL/photodiode) optics. II-VI acquisition (2024) made it a key integrated supplier. Investor relevance: core bottleneck supplier for both coherent and 400G/800G transceiver scaling.

nodes.name: Mitsubishi Electric Corp (Optics & Laser Division)
nodes.description: Japanese conglomerate with a major optoelectronics division supplying EML/DFB laser diodes, photodetectors, and optical components for datacenter, telecom, and industrial applications. Primary supplier to Japanese network equipment makers (NEC, Fujitsu) and global module integrators.

metrics.name: Mitsubishi Electric datacom laser share (EML/DFB, global)
metrics.description: Estimated 20% of global datacom EML/DFB laser supply, primarily serving Japanese network vendors and regional module makers; source: Yole semiconductor optics reports 2024–2025.

metrics.name: Mitsubishi Electric FY2025 consolidated revenue
metrics.description: Mitsubishi Electric FY2025 (ended March 2025) consolidated revenue ¥4.59 trillion; optics division is a smaller segment but strategically important for datacom.

nodes.notes: Mitsubishi Electric (Tokyo Stock Exchange: 6503.T) is a diversified manufacturer; optics division supplies Japanese vendors primarily but expanding global presence. Investor relevance: diversified exposure but optics/laser business benefits from AI datacenter growth.

nodes.name: Sumitomo Electric Industries Ltd. (Optics & Photonics Division)
nodes.description: Japanese diversified manufacturer with a major optics & photonics division supplying EML/DFB laser diodes, photodetectors, and fiber-optic subsystems for telecom and datacenter networks. Supplies to regional network equipment makers and global module integrators in Japan, Asia, and Europe.

metrics.name: Sumitomo Electric datacom laser share (EML/DFB, regional Asia-Pacific)
metrics.description: Estimated 15% share of EML/DFB datacom laser supply in Asia-Pacific region; primarily serving Japanese and regional telecom vendors; global share approximately 5–8%; source: Yole 2024–2025 market reports.

metrics.name: Sumitomo Electric FY2025 consolidated revenue
metrics.description: Sumitomo Electric FY2025 (ended March 2025) revenue ¥3.29 trillion; optics division contributes to telecom/datacenter segment.

nodes.notes: Sumitomo Electric (Tokyo Stock Exchange: 5802.T) is a major diversified manufacturer in Japan; optics division is well-established in Asian telecom markets but smaller global datacenter footprint than Lumentum or Coherent. Investor relevance: regional datacenter expansion exposure.

nodes.name: Innolight Technology Corp. (光迅科技)
nodes.description: Leading Chinese manufacturer of optical transceiver modules (400G, 800G, 1.6T) and subsystems. Supplies to Chinese hyperscalers (Alibaba, Tencent, Bytedance), international datacenter operators, and network equipment makers. Primary business: module assembly, integration, and test rather than laser-device manufacturing.

metrics.name: Innolight global optical transceiver module market share
metrics.description: Estimated 18% of global optical transceiver module market (2024–2025); fastest-growing supplier for 800G+ modules in hyperscaler deployments; source: Yole, SemiAnalysis datacom optics reports.

metrics.name: Innolight China datacenter module share
metrics.description: Estimated 35% market share of datacenter optical transceiver modules supplied to Chinese hyperscalers (Alibaba, Tencent, ByteDance); 2024–2025 data.

nodes.notes: Innolight (Shenzhen Stock Exchange: 300308.SZ) is a Chinese public company, major supplier of optical transceiver modules to hyperscalers. Business model: sources lasers (VCSEL, EML) and photodiodes from vendors, integrates and tests modules. Investor relevance: high exposure to Chinese and global datacenter buildout; competitive pricing and scale.

nodes.name: Eoptolink Technology Co., Ltd. (易飞扬)
nodes.description: Chinese optical transceiver module manufacturer specializing in 400G, 800G, and coherent modules for datacenter and telecom networks. Supplies to Chinese hyperscalers, international cloud providers, and network equipment makers. Competes with Innolight on cost and integration speed.

metrics.name: Eoptolink global optical transceiver module market share
metrics.description: Estimated 12% of global optical transceiver module market (2024–2025); growing presence in 800G+ coherent modules; source: Yole datacom optics market reports.

metrics.name: Eoptolink China datacenter module share
metrics.description: Estimated 22% market share of datacenter transceiver modules supplied within China; second player after Innolight; 2024–2025 data.

nodes.notes: Eoptolink (Shenzhen Stock Exchange: 300502.SZ) is a Chinese public company, emerging major supplier of optical modules. Sources laser and photodiode components from global suppliers, focuses on module integration and testing. Investor relevance: growth in coherent module demand; lower-cost alternative to Broadcom/Marvell.

edges.claim: Long-reach coherent optical transceiver modules require EML/DFB laser diodes as a core component; separate supply chain from short-reach 850nm VCSELs.
